disagreements.topic: October FOMC hike odds (agent_4 disputes the round-1 ~69%)
disagreements.positions: Round-1 supervisor and agents 1,2,3,5 (who adopted it): ~69% hike as of Sep 29, i.e. largely priced. agent_4: ~44% on DeFiRate's Sep 30 02:02 ET snapshot (Kalshi 44.5c, Polymarket 43.5c, ~$375k 24h volume), after a 21-point weekly drop.
disagreements.resolution: agent_4 is right; the round-1 69% was stale. ~69-71% was the level on Sep 28 / early Sep 29. On the afternoon of Sep 29, NY Fed President Williams said there was no immediate need to hike, and October odds fell to ~51% by the close (GuruFocus, 15:58 Sep 29) and to ~44% overnight (DeFiRate). The $75.95 close already reflects this. What it means: the Oct 28 decision is now close to a coin flip, not a largely priced hike, so the event is two-sided and a hold is the slight favourite. The next hike now looks more likely in December (~74% on DeFiRate). It is still variance, not a clear drift, for a 1-month ladder centred on spot.
disagreements.evidence: DeFiRate Fed decision odds (snapshot Sep 30 02:02 ET: hike 44%, hold 55%; Kalshi 66%->45% over the week); GuruFocus Sep 29 15:58 (51% from 71% after Williams); earlier path 52% Sep 17 (tech-insider), 56% Sep 20 (predictionmarketspicks).

one_month_reasoning: I kept the forecaster mean, which is centred on spot with a ~17% one-month sigma. The Oct 28 FOMC falls inside the window, but after Williams' Sep 29 remarks it is now close to 44-51% hike rather than 69%. That makes the event two-sided (a hold is slightly favoured), with no net drift. The late-October TI/NXP/STM prints also fall inside the window, and onsemi's own Q3 print (~Nov 2, unconfirmed) most likely falls just outside it.
confidence_reason: All five revised forecasts took up the round-1 corrections (net debt, capex-normalised FCF, FOMC date) and converged tightly: fair values $77-79, P(>=76) 0.51-0.525. The one fact I settled in round 2 (FOMC odds ~44-51%, not ~69%) changes the character of an in-window event but not the direction of the 12-month distribution, so I keep the mean.
thesis_break_reason: Agents are at $50-52 (mean ~$51.4). Below ~$52, ON trades ~11.5x CY27 consensus EPS ($4.53) and ~7-8% on normalised (~5%-capex) FCF, levels seen only near cycle troughs. Reaching that level would most likely take a guidance cut (auto/industrial relapse, utilisation or pricing reversal, SiC price war) or a failed or renegotiated Synaptics deal, rather than ordinary ~50-60% volatility noise.
key_drivers: Earnings recovery: Q2 2026 revenue $1,604M, non-GAAP EPS $0.74 above the guidance midpoint. Q3 guide $1.65-1.75B, 40-42% GM, $0.81-0.93 EPS. Consensus goes from CY26 $3.20 to CY27 $4.53, and ON trades ~16.8x CY27.
Normalised FCF: LTM FCF is flattered by trough capex (Q2 $34.3M, ~2% of sales). With capex at ~5%, 2027 FCF is ~$1.55-2.05B, which caps FCF-yield values at ~$75-80.
De-rating from the all-stock Synaptics deal (1.35x, 88/12 pro forma, close mid-2027) and back-loaded 2030 analyst-day targets (~$11B revenue, 53% GM).
SiC competition: Chinese wafers ~$400 vs ~$1,200 Western cost, and Czech job cuts. This is partly offset by two price increases in 2026, confirmed at the Aug 27 DB conference.

Rates: the Fed hiked in September. October hike odds fell from ~70% to ~44-51% on Sep 29-30 after Williams' remarks, with December now the likelier hike (~74%), so macro pressure on semi multiples is two-sided in the near term.

fair_value.reason: The round-2 agent fair values are $77-79 (mean $78), after all agents normalised capex (Q2 capex $34.3M, ~2% of sales), agent_2 fixed net debt ($0.595B) and cut its 19x multiple, and agent_4 dropped the Substack CY28 EPS. That is ~16.5-17.5x an NTM EPS of ~$4.5-5.0 and a ~5-5.5% yield on ~$1.6-2.0B normalised FCF. I found no further error, so I keep $78 (down from my round-1 $80), ~3% above spot.

summary: All five forecasters took up the round-1 corrections (capex-normalised FCF, agent_2's net debt and 19x multiple, agent_4's Substack EPS) and converged: fair values $77-79, median ~$78, P(close >= $76 on 2027-09-29) ~0.52, thesis break ~$52. The only open dispute was the October FOMC odds, and agent_4 was right: hike odds fell from ~70% to ~44-51% on Sep 29-30 after NY Fed President Williams' remarks, so the Oct 28 meeting is a two-sided coin flip rather than a priced-in hike. That adds variance but no direction, so I keep the forecaster mean ladders at low confidence. ON is a fairly valued high-beta cyclical recovery (~16.8x CY27) with the Q3 print (~Nov 2) and the mid-2027 Synaptics close ahead.
